gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-ethiopi: Wide, wiry and unmistakably technical, Nulshock stretches its outlined letters across the line. Noto Sans Ethiopic follows with sturdy, tall lowercase and hanging c terminals, so a long passage moves along without snagging.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-georgia: Noto Sans Georgian reads openly, its curves staying wide at the aperture and its ascender stems kept short on tall bodies. Nulshock's lack of any thick and thin is the standout.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-glagoli: Nulshock is stretched, bold and technical in outline. It excels at loud, spaced-out display lettering, while Noto Sans Glagolitic, a neutral sans-serif with open round letters, stays clear at small sizes.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Professional and modern, Noto Sans Gothic opens its lowercase counters wide like drilled glass beads beneath Nulshock's stretched, hairline-free heading. Shrink the heading and its spaced letters lose their punch.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Every stroke in Nulshock is cut to one width, giving it a stretched, wired look. But Noto Sans Grantha, a sans-serif, is the one built for reading, with tall little letters and bowls that never close up.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-gujarat: Nulshock stretches wide, with up and side strokes that look the same. Noto Sans Gujarati then carries a longer passage gently, its curved strokes ending early and its tall a, e and s staying open.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-gunjala: Stretched wire, bold and technical. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi sits below with crayon-tall lowercase and terminals cut back to a big gap, so text at a modest size looks best.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-gurmukh: Noto Sans Gurmukhi reads cleanly, its terminals pointing outward like tongs and its ascenders barely clearing the x-height. Nulshock glows above it like neon tubing.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Noto Sans Hanunoo fills most of its height with lowercase. Nulshock does loud, stretched display lettering best, while this sans-serif body handles continuous reading with easy open terminals.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Technical and bold, Nulshock ends every stroke at the same measured thickness. Noto Sans Hebrew, a sans-serif, does the quieter work, with a dominant midsection and wide gaps between curve ends and stems.
